newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's party boss blasts Stoiber for EMU debate.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's party boss blasts Stoiber for EMU debate.

text.p: The general secretary of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats criticised Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber on Tuesday for his calls to postpone Europe's single currency if it is not hard enough.
Peter Hintze told the Cologne daily Express that speculating about delaying monetary union could endanger the whole project.

"It's not correct to play the timetable and the stability criteria off against one another," Hintze said. "On the contrary, the fixed start date for the euro has led to higher price stability among future currency union members."
The single currency is due to be launched on January 1, 1999. Countries wishing to join the currency union must fulfil financial criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
Stoiber, a senior member of the CDU's sister party, the Christian Social Union, has repeatedly called for a strict interpretation of the stability criteria and said they must determine the timetable.
In the latest in a barrage of recent interviews, he told Monday's edition of the Financial Times that a "controlled delay" would be better than launching a weak currency.
